title: A three-part refactor across two sessions
goal: Split a report.js monolith into parse, format and render modules over two agent sessions. End session 1 with a HANDOFF.md, start session 2 from it, and finish with every constraint intact.
setup_cmd: cp -r exercises/ex-2-2-long-task/starter ~/fm-ex/ex-2-2-long-task && cd ~/fm-ex/ex-2-2-long-task && git init -q && git add -A && git commit -qm base && npm i

starter_prompts.claude: We are refactoring src/report.js in 3 parts: (1) parse.js, (2) format.js, (3) render.js, with report.js left as a thin facade. Constraints: generateReport(csv) output stays byte-identical, never edit test/fixtures/, no new dependencies, plain ESM. Do part 1 only: make test/part1-parse.test.js pass and keep `npm test` otherwise unchanged. Then write HANDOFF.md with ## Done, ## Next and ## Constraints so a fresh session can continue without this chat. Commit.
starter_prompts.codex: We are refactoring src/report.js in 3 parts: (1) parse.js, (2) format.js, (3) render.js, with report.js left as a thin facade. Then write HANDOFF.md with ## Done, ## Next and ## Constraints so a fresh session can continue without this chat. Commit.

solution_notes: The constraints live in HANDOFF.md as well as in the prompt. A constraint stated only in chat is the first thing a summary drops or a new session never sees.
HANDOFF.md is written for a reader with zero memory: what is done, the exact next steps in order, the constraints, and gotchas such as the trailing newline in the golden output.
Session 2 starts fresh (Claude Code /clear or a new process, Codex /new or a new process) and its first prompt is 'Read HANDOFF.md and continue with Next', so nothing depends on compaction quality.
One commit per part gives a safe rollback point and lets the next session see the state with git log instead of trusting a summary.
